scope: Traditional standalone loginUi source-authored button/menu/select/toggle action execution and reLoginView/upLoginData callbacks; exact current product consumer against locked original. No browser/WebJS/v2, TTS or engine/store reselection.

baseline.sourceOrigin: exact read-only git show blobs; later root C3 integration does not change this snapshot

originalContract.contract: A source row action runs in Fragment lifecycleScope IO. Absolute URL follows existing external navigation (excluded here). JS action concatenates getLoginJs + newline + action, binds java=SourceLoginJsExtensions, result=getLoginData real Java Map, actual book/chapter, isLongClick. Standalone caller has null book/chapter. It does not call login() implicitly, use action return as headers, or pre-store loginInfo. name is diagnostic only. A null action is skipped; a blank loginUrl yields null loginJS and skips JS action. Cancellation is rechecked before ordinary error logging; Android has no matching fixed30s timer.

Snapshot begins with complete viewModel.loginInfo then overwrites visible text/password edits only, preserving hidden keys and explicit empty strings. Startup uses stored map, not derived defaults. Select/toggle update transient map before their action; ordinary text edit is read when snapshot is taken.

Select ignores initialization callback; real selection sets working value then invokes optional action(false). Button accessibility click is false; touch release >666ms sets isLongClick, with200ms dedupe. Toggle cycles the exact declared chars including empty strings before invoking action with corresponding long flag. Same helper handles source menus composed from these rows.

Weak callback reaches same UI owner on main. reLoginView(deltaUp=false) renders source loginUi; refreshExplore aliases reUiView(false) in this host. Dynamic re-render preserves previous rows on failure. deltaUp=true reuses/moves existing named controls and returns before rebuilding/evaluating reused controls; it is not a whole-form reload.

Transient reset rebuilds VM Map from current text/password defaults-or-empty and toggle/select default-or-first choices; hidden keys are removed. Button only resets display, never becomes credential entry. Select uses safe index; no immediate source.putLoginInfo call.

Each value becomes nullable toString; first same-name row is found. Text/password update working map+actual input, button updates display only, toggle updates working char+display, select sets adapter selection and relies on existing listener for map/action behavior. Unknown/hidden keys update transient map with null-to-empty. Programmatic text/select updates may schedule the original watchers/listeners; cannot replace this with blind persistent Map merge.

Explicit OK follows login action even when button rows exist. Non-v2 dismiss with !oKToClose && hasChange persists the VM map or clears if empty; text editing alone does not itself mark hasChange. Dismiss removes Handler callbacks. Action is Fragment-lifecycle scoped, not renderJob; do not claim onDestroyView synchronously cancels every legacy action.

findings.title: New original-rendered controls still execute source actions through the old JSC consumer
currentEvidence: View:56-65 routes onAction to handleButton for every source
View:632-650 calls runButtonJS without original source branch
View:754-873 creates a fresh JSCoreEngine and SourceScriptThread task
OriginalTraditionalRuntime:38-51 admits loginUi/formLogin but no row-action operation
Package runtime:314-332 and Preview operation enum:308-326 have no row-action DTO/API
findings.trigger: Any non-URL action on a traditional rendered button/select/toggle, including dynamic source settings menus.
findings.impact: Action does not use the source actor/existing native task/original Rhino/Java Map identity that now owns render and explicit form login. Plain result is a JSC object and isLongClick is absent.
findings.minimumFix: Add a bounded original row-action operation/API/result to the existing runtime/executor/service and route only traditional actions through it. Reuse finite source login host, original evaluator, same source revision/owner/deadline/cancel/effects. Skip JS for original null loginJS/action and ignore its completion; no browser fallback.

findings.title: Selection and action entry can overwrite stored credentials with a reduced/defaulted map before the action
currentEvidence: View:60-63 select setter calls persistCurrentFormValues before onAction
View:642-649 handleButton stores currentFormValues before JS
View:653-678 currentFormValues starts empty, excludes hidden entries, resolves empty text to default, then writes Keychain
Dialog:791-829 performs no equivalent pre-store
findings.trigger: Stored {hidden:token,username:old}, visible username edited to empty with nonempty default, then select/button action. Current reduced snapshot drops hidden and restores default, writes it before evaluating the action; the original passes hidden plus empty to result and keeps raw storage untouched.
findings.impact: Loss of existing hidden credential/state fields and unintended persistent writes, even for an action that fails or only changes presentation.
findings.minimumFix: For traditional actions use the existing originalFormSubmissionValues complete snapshot and bypass select/action automatic storeLoginInfo. Ordinary selector/toggle edits stay in the same transient values state; persistence requires its original explicit/dismiss contract.

findings.title: upLoginData currently mutates persistent credentials instead of the actual form state
currentEvidence: View:993-1006 converts map to dictionary and merges it into loginOwner Keychain
No values/fields/labels update occurs in that handler
OriginalSourceLoginHost:32 is typed unsupported for actual original form-login host
Dialog:130-217 implements current-control-specific transient update/reset
findings.trigger: java.upLoginData(null), a visible input/button/select update, or a hidden key update from a source action.
findings.impact: Null reset is a no-op; visible controls remain stale; button presentation can become a persistent credential key; changes are durably stored earlier than original permits. Native host does not yet support this callback at all.
findings.minimumFix: A callback-capable finite task/host must report typed ordered UI updates to the same form owner. Implement null reset, first-row matching, per-type value/display behavior and select listener/watcher consequences; never treat it as direct Keychain merge.

findings.title: reLoginView is a separate JSC reload and cannot represent deltaUp
currentEvidence: LegadoJSBridge:218/1817-1821 exposes parameterless reLoginView only
View:784-806 invokes evaluateJsLoginUiResult using a new JSC evaluator and reconstructs values from stored map
View:835-848 reruns labels on the action engine instead of per-original-row fresh evaluation
OriginalSourceLoginHost:33-34 typed unsupported for native refresh
findings.trigger: Action updates source variables/working form, then java.reLoginView(true) or java.refreshExplore().
findings.impact: deltaUp is lost, current transient edits can be replaced by stale stored values, native source pipeline is bypassed, and reused original rows/labels are reevaluated or rebuilt.
findings.minimumFix: Same original UI owner consumes explicit typed refresh request, preserving current complete working snapshot. delta false can call existing typed render; delta true must preserve/move reused controls and avoid evaluating their labels again. Failure keeps valid prior rows.

findings.title: Original row actions lack long-click context and an owned cancel/publication lifecycle
currentEvidence: Grid:27-28 exposes only field callbacks, with no long flag
Grid:84-95 button/toggle use plain tap
View:764 detached task is not assigned to any owned action handle
View:149-154 cancels only formSubmissionTask/render task
View:799-806/846-848/871 applies asynchronous action callbacks without render generation/dismissal guard
findings.trigger: A source branches on isLongClick, or a held action/refresh callback finishes after sheet dismissal or a newer action/render.
findings.impact: Long-press branch cannot run; obsolete actions may continue making owner changes and publish stale UI. No actual device race is asserted, but the unowned path is directly reachable in source.
findings.minimumFix: Add original-row long flag and one same-owner action task/generation, cancellation propagation and effect-preserving terminal errors. Do not claim immediate onDestroyView cancellation parity: original actions are Fragment-lifecycle scoped.

findings.title: Traditional row actions bypass the sensitive task/error/log boundary established for render and form confirmation
currentEvidence: View:633 logs authored action verbatim
View:815-832 logs raw action/state/error for a source-name branch
View:859-871 displays and logs raw engine/API error details
LegadoRuntime.kt:80/129 sensitive protection currently names only loginUi/formLogin
findings.trigger: A traditional action derives an error/response from its synthetic password/token, or embeds sensitive data in the action/state text.
findings.impact: The newly original-rendered action can expose raw secret-derived details through its legacy logging/UI path; the native safe error boundary is never entered.
findings.minimumFix: New operation must activate existing sensitive RuntimeTask before any evaluation, reuse existing parser/HTTP diagnostic seam and expose only static error code/effect metadata. Do not copy legacy action/body/error logging into the new path.

adjacentExplicitlyDeferred.fact: Original text/password action runs after600ms changed-value debounce with initialization excluded; current Grid edits never invoke those actions. Record as adjacent trigger work, not silently included in this button/select/toggle-only first execution slice.

Current button-containing toolbar branch persists reduced currentFormValues and dismisses instead of original OK login action. Full hasChange/oKToClose dismissal persistence has not been migrated. A safe action slice must not imply this whole lifecycle is complete.
